A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MINTO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Atari experiments in online, offline and distributional RL, continuous-control experiments, and operator ablations, with additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds further algorithm comparisons, IQN architecture experiments, and Car-on-the-Hill value-estimation diagnostics in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core MINTO update remains unchanged. However, Algorithm 2 changes the specified IQN target from target-network quantiles alone to the minimum of online and target quantiles at the selected action. Appendix B also introduces a critic-specific integration for CrossQ+WN. These are limited procedural changes; the PDFs do not establish whether the IQN revision reflects changed code or corrected pseudocode.

E1.justification: v2 adds the deterministic Car-on-the-Hill task, with continuous states and discrete actions, in Appendix E. The original Atari and continuous-control task sets remain. Offline appendix captions change from 15 to 14 games, correcting the description of existing coverage rather than documenting a removed game.

E2.justification: v1's offline experiments compare CQL with CQL+MINTO; v2 adds Double CQL, FR-CQL, ScCQL and Maxmin CQL in Figure 6 and Appendix D. It also adds CrossQ+WN and FR-SimbaV1/V2 comparisons in Appendix D.6. These substantially expand comparator membership. Maxmin DQN was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: 3,000 training episodes, a 10-by-10 state grid evaluated under both actions, depth-50 search for reference values, and measurements of value error, bias and training loss. Section 5.2 additionally tests IQN with IMPALA and LayerNorm. These are substantial protocol additions; the existing settings in Tables 1–6 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's operator ablations and selection-frequency analysis are retained. New Appendix E directly investigates estimation bias, value error and learning instability, including an Online Only comparison, addressing the proposed mechanism beyond return measurements. Figure 4 also extends selection-frequency monitoring to the IMPALA configuration.

E5.justification: The SimbaV2 MuJoCo caption changes from 5 seeds in v1 Figure 13 to 10 in v2 Figure 18, matching the existing main-text reporting. This does not establish additional runs. New Figures 35–36 specify 100 seeds with IQM or mean estimates and 95% confidence intervals; the general uncertainty-reporting practice is retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for offline comparators, CrossQ+WN, functional regularization and value-estimation diagnostics. Figure 6 shows Maxmin CQL outperforming CQL+MINTO, with further improvement from Maxmin CQL+MINTO. Figure 4 adds an approximately 10% IQN AUC advantage with IMPALA. The reported DQN AUC advantages in Section 5.1 also change from approximately 18%/24% to 17%/22% for CNN/IMPALA.

T1.justification: Section 3 changes the formal reward model from a real-valued reward function to a reward distribution. Corollary 1, its assumptions and the complete non-expansion proof in Appendix A are otherwise unchanged; no new convergence theorem is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: minimum-based online/target bootstrapping mitigates overestimation, supports faster stable learning, and applies broadly with negligible overhead. Added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific interpretations: conservative ensemble updates can be advantageous offline because exploration is less consequential, and incorporating online estimates can increase variance. Appendix B discusses alternative critic-specific targets and leaves their systematic comparison open. The original concerns about underestimation and exploration remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code is released and supplies a MINTO repository link plus implementation provenance for the discrete online and offline experiments. Appendix E adds detailed network, optimizer, replay, exploration and reference-value construction settings. This substantially expands reproducibility information, although repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: Related work adds explicit positioning against clipped Double Q-learning and Kapturowski et al.'s trust-region approach. Additional citations support the new diagnostics and implementation provenance. These extend the existing discussion without substantially changing MINTO's positioning relative to target-free methods and ensembles.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 consolidates paragraphs, edits terminology and grammar, updates publication and affiliation text, and reorganizes Appendix D with additional subsections. The scientific additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is expanded to display both CNN and IMPALA results. v2 adds an offline comparison figure, extensive per-task comparison plots, and the multi-panel bias/error/loss Figures 35–36. Existing figures are largely retained or relocated, with some caption, legend and axis refinements; the six hyperparameter tables remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly supports its bias and stability explanation through return comparisons; v2 adds direct value-error, bias and loss diagnostics in Appendix E. New offline and actor–critic comparator checks address important gaps, while code-access information improves reproducibility documentation. Together these substantially strengthen the paper's empirical support, including evidence of a stronger ensemble baseline. The diagnostic remains limited to a small deterministic task, and some broad performance claims remain insufficiently qualified.
